chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

Isa ibn Ja'far ibn Isa asked Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) about a woman who breastfed a boy for me, asking: Is it permissible for me to marry the daughter of her husband? He said to me: 'How good is what you asked from here! It is assumed that people will say: His wife is forbidden to him because of the milk of the stallion (sire). This is the milk of the stallion, nothing else.' I said to him: 'Indeed, the girl is not the daughter of the woman who breastfed for me; she is the daughter of another.' He said: 'Even if there were ten [daughters] scattered [from different sources], nothing would be permissible for you from them, and they would be in the position of your daughters.'

key_terms.لَبَنُ الْفَحْلِ: Milk of the sire (referring to the husband's milk or the milk he 'produced' through his wife)

ai.seo_question: Does breast milk from a woman make her husband's daughters forbidden to the man who fed her child?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibition of 'laban al-fahl' (milk of the sire) extends to the husband's daughters, rendering them forbidden to the man as if they were his own biological daughters. He emphasizes the comprehensiveness of this ruling by noting that even if the daughters are from different mothers, they remain prohibited, illustrating the broad application of milk kinship in Shia jurisprudence.
